stem: A static field differs from an instance field how?
options: ONE value shared by the whole class, not one per object
explanation: Three Counter objects each have their own Id, but all share one _created. Reached via the class name: Counter.Created.

stem: What can you NOT do with a static class like Math?
explanation: A static class is a bag of functions - no instances, ever. Math, Console and File all work this way.

stem: When does a static constructor run?
options: Every time an object is made
Automatically, exactly once, before the class is first used
explanation: No modifier, no parameters, never called by you - the runtime guarantees exactly one execution before first touch.

stem: A Car with a private Engine field is an example of:
explanation: HAS-A, not IS-A. The car is BUILT FROM parts - and new Car("Leaf", new ElectricEngine(150)) swaps the part at run time, which inheritance never can.

stem: "Favour composition over inheritance" mainly because composition is:
options: Looser - swap parts at run time, mix many, test with fakes
explanation: Inheritance locks one base at compile time and couples you to everything in it. Composition takes only what you need and can be handed a fake for testing.

stem: Game's constructor takes an ILogger instead of creating a ConsoleLogger inside. The payoff?
options: Game can be tested with a MemoryLogger - no console, no noise - and rewired without edits
explanation: Injected dependencies are visible and swappable. new-ing them inside welds the class to one implementation forever.

stem: Why is static MUTABLE data a testing problem?
options: It is global state: tests interfere with each other, and nothing can swap it for a fake
explanation: One shared value leaks between tests and hides in no signature. Static shines for PURE functions (Math.Sqrt); be suspicious of static data.

stem: "Depend on ILogger, not ConsoleLogger" is which SOLID principle?
explanation: D - depend on abstractions, not concretions. 2.13 treats all five properly.

stem: Which is the correct way to read a static property?
explanation: Static members are reached through the CLASS name. Instance-reference access does not even compile in C#.

stem: When IS inheritance still the right call?
options: When the child is genuinely a KIND of the parent and you want its behaviour
explanation: IS-A plus wanted behaviour = inheritance (Dog : Animal). Reuse alone = composition. The test is the sentence, not the convenience.
